source.citation: Nguyen MT, Martignier T & Pannell JR (2024). Widespread male sterility and trioecy in androdioecious Mercurialis annua: Its distribution, genetic basis, and estimates of morph-specific fitness components. American Journal of Botany 111:e16429
sections: Methods: Expression of sexual phenotypes in a common garden
source.source_access: Authoritative primary open PMC HTML and original Table 1/2 text; supplementary DOCX link and Figshare file unavailable due network restrictions

taxon.name: Mercurialis annua
taxon.sexual_structures: Hermaphrodite bears male and female unisexual flowers on same plant; male-sterile female has nonfunctional male flowers
taxon.geography: southern Spain (Motril) parental seed source common garden, not continentwide random material

female_phenotype_retains_male_looking_no.source_location: Original 2024 Discussion 'Widespread trioecy in hexaploid M. annua'
female_phenotype_retains_male_looking_no.observation: Females are phenotypically monoecious and produce sterile male-looking flowers that otherwise resemble fertile male flowers on hermaphrodites; they can be missed in morphological field counts
female_phenotype_retains_male_looking_no.implication: Morphological retention of staminate organ is NOT proof of pollen fertility or same genetic structure as true dioecy

distance_experiment.year: Common garden prior to published 2024 study, Motril-derived plants
distance_experiment.response_definition: Number of female flowers that DID NOT develop fruits divided by total female flowers on each plant; interpreted as pollen limitation proxy, not measured stigma pollen grains
distance_experiment.proxy_observation_warning: Non-development of fruit was inferred to indicate no pollination; resource-related fruit failure and mate identity cannot be excluded without direct pollen and fertilization data

reported_linear_mixed_model.response: proportion of undeveloped female flowers; printed Table 2 linear mixed model on plant-level proportion

distance_by_morph_interaction.reason_dropped: No detected sex-specific difference in distance slope; source reports dropped after AIC comparison

seed_biomass_followup.response: Seed biomass / plant biomass (as reported in Table 2; model scale is not independently reconstructed)
seed_biomass_followup.conclusion: No detected difference in measured seed-biomass endpoint by morph or distance; NOT a zero causal effect or same-cohort compensation identified

design_confounds: Center group contains four male pollen sources AND four hermaphrodites and females; ring hermaphrodites themselves may emit pollen, so distance is an ecological proximity treatment not pure exclusive male pollen source
Three replicate assemblies with plants nested in each; 71 plants analyzed of 84 planted, missing 13 original individual data not accessed
Female flower non-fruit output is an indirect pollen-limitation proxy
All morphs were already present in arrays; no invasion when rare or genotype-based parentage tracked

separate_morph_common_garden.site: Motril parental seed source grown in pot common garden separate from 0.5/1.5 m distance experiment
separate_morph_common_garden.design: Three blocks of 70 pots, each pot planted with one male, female, hermaphrodite; total 210 pots and 630 initially placed plants

male_vs_hermaphrodite_male_effort_ratio.source_report: Original authors report ratio based on male-flower biomass/aboveground biomass, NOT actual paternal genotypes or pollen germination

separate_morph_common_garden.authors_power_statement: Study reports approximate 80% power for detecting >12% female relative seed difference; this is not proof that gain <12% or an equivalence study
separate_morph_common_garden.striking_source_inconsistency: Source main text t=2.91 df=213 p=.097 for seed count per biomass cannot be simultaneously correct; t=2.91 would have two-sided p≈.004, while source coefficient 4.35 with CI[-.76,9.46] includes zero and corresponds to t≈1.68 and p≈.095. Do not choose a corrected t without raw data or author erratum.

independent_original_population_survey_a.model_result: Model requires a restoration cost greater than zero in its parameter settings to maintain trioecy, but biological identity and actual fitness cost of linked restorers remain unmeasured
independent_original_population_survey_a.original_author_conclusion: Trioecy possible without pollen limitation when genotype-specific restoration costs and mating parameters satisfy prior simulation conditions

limitations: Directly verified primary 2024 Table 2 coefficients and 95% CIs; numerical predictions are re-expression of fitted published linear model at 0.5 and 1.5 m, NOT new data fits or actual individual observations
Fruit failure proxy cannot isolate failure of pollen receipt from resource-mediated fruit abortion, although original authors interpret it as pollen limitation
Distance effect p<.001 and female offset p=.029 support original source-specific associations, but interaction p=.80 does not prove exactly equal slopes across morphs
CIs of each printed coefficient cannot be combined to produce correct CI for a full 0.5/1.5m prediction without covariance of fitted coefficients
No detected seed biomass response does not establish absence of fitness costs or compensatory seed maturation
Separate common garden has 383 female-function and 201 male-function analyzed plant outcomes; not same 71 distance experiment plants and not 109 field population records
Original printed seed-count-per-biomass model narrative t=2.91 p=.097 is internally statistically inconsistent; no fabricated correction chosen
Original 2024 authors' >12% detectable difference power statement is NOT a confidence bound or proof that femaleness lacks any benefit
Model restorer cost rho=.15-.4 is an assumed simulation regime chosen to match morph frequencies, not measured cost or a source-calibrated SLK module K
Full 109-pop supplement S1, 3-year count supplement S2, 64-cross S3 and 39-cross S4 not downloaded; raw data analysis not performed
No same-plant genotype-specific paternity, maternal genetic transmission, CMS allele or rare mutant invasion fitness measured
No SLK Phi, g0, Delta_R nor full joint fitness calculated from this published source
